text:
rachel: Heads-up — customers are hitting ~4x baseline 5xxs and timeouts across hosted inference since the 09:00 deploy. Most reports show gateway 502/504; billing meter showing unexpected token bursts for a few tenants. 

sam: Seen it. Dashboard at https://internal.redwood/infra/5xx spikes. Is this the staged rollout?

joel: Yep, deploy id: release/stage-2026-03-18-09. Canary was 12% traffic. I can see a config change to the routing selector and a new feature flag 'stage-prefetch-window-ms'.

rachel: Customers started calling after 09:25. Repro from their side: single sync request times out after ~8s then gateway 502. Sharing curl sample I ran:

rachel: ```bash
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -d '{"model":"rwd-8b","prompt":"hi"}' https://api.redwood-hosted/v1/generate
# -> 502 Bad Gateway, upstream read error
```

ops-bot: Alert: canary-traffic (release/stage-2026-03-18-09) 502-rate +250% over 5m. Triggered pager to oncall.

maria: My read — the 'stage-prefetch-window-ms' default got set to 0 in the canary config; that disables prefix prefetching and causes a thundering K/V cache miss pattern under short-lived connections. Looks like a timing leak where batching expects a positive prefetch window.

sam: If that's the root cause, we should flip the flag to the previous value for canary only. Can we patch without a full rollback? Need coordination: support comms + deploy rollback window.

joel: Patch command (canary-only):
```bash
redwoodctl config set --release release/stage-2026-03-18-09 --scope canary stage-prefetch-window-ms=50
```
I'm hitting permission denied from the console (403). Could someone with config-admin flip it?

maria: I can do it. Before I patch — what's the impact window if we keep canary at 12%? Any high-value tenants in that slice?

support-team: Affected tenants: acme-corp, beta-ml, quickchat. Beta-ml and QuickChat are high QPS and reported timeouts. Acme reported billing spike traces — likely retries.

maria: Applying the canary patch now.

maria: ```
$ redwoodctl config set --release release/stage-2026-03-18-09 --scope canary stage-prefetch-window-ms=50
Applied config to canary slice (id: canary-12).
```

ops-bot: DeployBot: config change applied to release/stage-2026-03-18-09 (canary-12). Event id: evt-7823456-01.

joel: I'm seeing 5xx rate dropping in the canary slice metrics. Overall cluster 5xx still elevated but trending down.

rachel: Support to customers: posting interim note "investigating elevated 5xx and timeouts; mitigation applied to canary, working on global rollback if required." Also started refund/billing hold for acme-corp.

sam: Can we run a targeted smoke test for the canary after the patch? I'll run 200 requests at normal concurrency against canary tag.

sam: ```bash
for i in {1..200}; do curl -s -H "X-Canary: canary-12" -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -d '{"model":"rwd-8b","prompt":"smoke"}' https://api.redwood-hosted/v1/generate &
done
wait
```

sam: Results: 200 requests -> 0 failures, median latency 180ms. Good.

joel: Recommend hold on the rollout until we validate stage-prefetch-window in staging for a longer window. We should also add a guard to the rollout pipeline to block zero-ms values for prefetch keys.

maria: Agreed. I'll open a PR to add validation and backfill a migration to set safe defaults for any releases that accidentally had 0.

rachel: Confirming with customers that the immediate issue is mitigated for canary. Still want an org rollback play if overall 5xx doesn't normalize by +30m.

ops-bot: Monitor: global 5xx trending down (-65% in last 10m).

sam: I'll stay on-call for 1h to watch metrics and help rollback if needed.

joel: Postmortem owner: joel. Tentative action items: gated config validation, migration for safe defaults, improve canary targeting visibility, update runbook for timing-leak patterns.

rachel: Thanks. I'll follow up with affected customers and open a billing incident for acme-corp.

support-team: Noted. Updating customers now. :white_check_mark:

maria: Closing this thread if metrics stay good. Ping me if new 5xx appear.

rachel: Thanks team. :pray:
